title.narrative: Onfarm conservation of the declining plant species in Mayuge destrict

description.narrative: Farmers in the Mayuge district of Uganda are increasingly relying on monoculture sugarcane cultivation that depend on adapted plant species. Monocultural farming systems reduce plant diversity and threaten native plant species. To counteract, the IKI Small Grants project has strengthened the conservation of declining native plants through natural resource management for 250 households. The project identified and documented threatened native plants and prioritised them for propagation using improved agricultural practices. Smallholder farmers have been supported to establish community seed banks, tree nurseries, and backyard gardens, cultivating indigenous plants. In addition, the project improved the availability, accessibility, and sustainable use of these plants by promoting their use through radio posts and print campaigns. A dialogue with communal policy makers has been initiated to formulate on-farm biodiversity conservation ordinances and to politically anchor project interventions.
